A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Presto and LongTake-HD work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations, a human preference study, model and data ablations, and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds dataset-quality measurements, caption-similarity comparisons, and ablation consistency scores.

M1.justification: The progressive-caption procedure, three SCA variants, chosen OSCA mechanism, Allegro/T5 architecture, and EMA-VFI interpolation remain unchanged. Added explanations and analyses do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 3.3 newly evaluates Panda-70M and HD-VILA-100M videos alongside LongTake-HD for dataset-quality assessment; v1 discussed these datasets without reporting this comparison. The reported training corpus and video-generation task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix B/Table 6 adds unrefined Vanilla captions as a comparator to progressive captions. Generation comparisons retain Gen-3, Allegro, TALC, and, in the user study, Merge Videos.

E3.justification: v2 adds Overall Consistency to the existing 360p/40-frame ablation evaluation. New protocols include 100 sampled videos per dataset with four-point human ratings, and cosine similarity, ROUGE-L, and BLEU-4 comparisons with inference captions held fixed. Existing training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a text-level diagnostic testing whether progressive refinement brings training captions closer to inference captions. Section 5.4 extends existing component ablations with consistency measurements. A direct model-training comparison of caption styles is explicitly deferred.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated model runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing annotation counts are retained, and the added results continue point-estimate reporting without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results include dataset quality ratings of 2.80/2.31/2.18 for LongTake-HD/HD-VILA/Panda, consistency scores of 25.29/25.06/24.88 for OSCA/SSCA/ISCA, and vanilla/progressive caption similarity of 0.6408/0.7778 (v2 Tables 1, 4, 6). Existing generation, user-study, and original ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The temporal partition definitions, attention constructions, and overlap condition are retained. New caption and dynamics arguments are informal interpretations, without added mathematical derivations, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain coherent, content-rich 15-second generation, parameter-free SCA, and the 261k-video LongTake-HD dataset. The headline 78.5 Semantic Score and 100 Dynamic Degree claims are unchanged; the conclusion reiterates the existing importance of curated data.

C2.justification: Appendix B links closer training/inference caption distributions to semantic quality while acknowledging that direct training validation remains future work. Appendix C proposes motion blur and compression during data preparation and output encoding as causes of quality loss. Existing fidelity, artifact, and still-frame limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that VBench evaluates the original 88 frames before interpolation, explains the human rating criteria, and identifies H.264 encoding. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that the existing experiments were rerun or their settings changed.

R1.justification: A new related-work paragraph discusses Phenaki and VideoPoet, distinguishing Presto through its combined dataset, model, and interpolation pipeline. Four additional citations support caption richness and text-similarity metrics. Previously cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and grammar edits, adds Section 3.3 and Appendices B–C, and updates cross-references while retaining the main narrative structure. Appendix C introduces a redundant opening with an unfinished sentence.

P2.justification: v2 adds two tables and a consistency column to the ablation table. VBench formatting changes from highlighting the Presto row to marking best and second-best scores. Existing figures are retained, with tables and appendix material relocated as text expands.

improvement.justification: The dataset comparison and added consistency measurements strengthen support for the existing contributions, while evaluation disclosures and ranking formatting improve transparency. The gains are limited: caption similarity provides indirect evidence, the compression explanation remains untested, and Appendix C contains redundant prose.
